{{short description|American number theorist (b.1965)}}
'''Judy Holdener''' (née Newhauser) is an American [[mathematician]] and [[educator]]. She is a professor of mathematics at [[Kenyon College]]. She was born in 1965. Holdener's primary interest is in [[number theory]]. She discovered a simpler proof of the theorem of [[Jacques Touchard|Touchard]], which states that every [[perfect number]] is of the form 2k, 12k+1, or 36k+9.

Holdener earned her B.S. in mathematics at [[Kent State University]] and her M.S. and Ph.D. in mathematics at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]]. Holdener joined the faculty of Kenyon College in 1997, where she is currently the John B. McCoy Distinguished Teaching Chair.

The poem ''Euler's Daughter'' by award-winning South African poet [[Athol Williams]] is dedicated to Holdener in celebration of her love of mathematics and life.<ref>{{Cite web| title=A Reading of Poetry with Mathematics | url=http://scholarship.claremont.edu/jhm/poetry_reading_2013.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160811054628/http://scholarship.claremont.edu/jhm/poetry_reading_2013.pdf | archive-date=2016-08-11}}</ref>
